summary.text: Tropical climates make up group A, the first of the five major groups in the Köppen system, and their coolest month averages 18 °C (64 °F) or more.
They stay hot and humid all year with a very small yearly temperature range, and normally have just two seasons: a wet one and a dry one.
How much rain falls in the driest month splits them into three types: tropical rainforest (Af), tropical monsoon (Am) and tropical savanna (Aw or As).

facts.label: Köppen letter
facts.value: A, the first of five major groups

facts.label: Usual seasons
facts.value: Two: a wet season and a dry season

facts.label: Rainforest driest month
facts.value: At least 60 mm (2.4 in) of rain

items.prompt: A humid coastal city has steamy summers, but its coldest month averages 16 °C. Would the Köppen system class it as tropical?

options.label: No, its coolest month is below the 18 °C line
Yes, because its summers are hot and humid
Yes, because it sits on a warm ocean coast
No, because tropical places get no humidity

items.explain: Köppen counts a climate as tropical only when even its coolest month averages 18 °C or more, so hot summers are not enough.

items.prompt: Two places are both hot and humid all year. What does Köppen look at to decide whether one is rainforest and the other savanna?

options.label: The average heat of the hottest month
How much rain falls in the driest month
How far each one lies from the sea
How tall the trees grow in each one

items.explain: All three tropical types are told apart by the precipitation of the driest month.

items.prompt: Someone moves from a city with cold winters to a tropical region. What will they most likely notice about temperature over the year?

options.label: Winters there turn bitterly cold
Spring and autumn swing wildly
It barely changes from month to month
It drops steadily every single year

items.explain: Tropical climates have a very small yearly temperature range, so the months feel much alike.

items.prompt: In many tropical places, much of the plant life keeps growing right through the year. Why?

options.label: Because the soil is always volcanic
Because no insects live there to eat it
Because days get longer in winter
Because it is hot and rain is plentiful

items.explain: High temperatures and abundant rainfall let much of the plant life grow throughout the year.

items.prompt: A tropical rainforest is packed with trees. What do all those trees do to the humidity of the air around them?

options.label: They dry it by soaking water out of the air
They add to it as water evaporates from them
They have no effect on it at all
They lower it by blocking falling rain

items.explain: Through transpiration, water evaporates from the surface of living plants into the air, which feeds the climate's humidity.

items.prompt: Rainforest plants grow in stacked layers and take many different growth forms. What does this help them get?

options.label: Room for their roots
Shelter from the wind
Enough sunlight
Distance from animals

items.explain: Vegetation under the rainforest climate develops vertical layers and varied growth forms to receive enough sunlight.
